thread:
jamie: Quick sync — planning a canary rollout tonight for the serving runtime: kernel 3.1.0 + quant-profile v0.9. Target window 22:00 UTC, 30m. Need deployment owner, smoke checks, and rollback ready.

alex: Are we canarying by region or by instance class? also any model compatibility notes?

sam: My notes: quant v0.9 changes padding handling for KV cache; should be fine for all models but watch small-llama variants for perf regression.

keith: I can own the deploy and be on-call for the window. Will be online 21:45–23:30 UTC.

rhett: suggestion: canary = 5% traffic in us-west1 and eu-west1, 5 machines each (n1-standard-ish). If green -> ramp to 25% then full.

ops-bot: CI check passed: runtime-build: success, smoke-tests: queued. (link: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234)

jamie: thanks keith. smoke checklist I suggest:
- preflight: ensure monitoring alert hooks and synthetic tests are green
- deploy: apply kernel/quant change to canary pool
- run targeted smoke: 1000 short requests across chat/generation + embeddings small set
- validate: p95 latency within 10% of baseline, error rate < 0.1%
- rollback if >10% latency regression or any 5xx spike

jamie: quick commands for deploy:
```bash
# promote new image to canary pool
kubectl set image deploy/runtime-canary runtime-container=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:3.1.0-quant-v0.9 --namespace=redwood-serving-canary
# wait for rollout
kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime-canary --namespace=redwood-serving-canary --watch
```

keith: smoke script I'll run (local):
```bash
python tools/smoke_runner.py --target http://canary-lb.redwood-serving-canary --requests 1000 --models gpt-small,embed-64 --concurrency 20
```

alex: pinging infra: any kernel-level node-drain considerations? we should disable auto-scaler during window.

rhett: noted. I'll set cluster autoscaler to manual during window and annotate nodes. Also will temp bump log retention for extra traces.

sam: watch these metrics during smoke: token/sec, p95 generation latency, kv-cache hit rate, CPU stall %, and OOM events. If kv-cache hit rate drops -> obvious regression.

keith: I'll keep a deploy runbook open. Rollback command if needed:
```bash
# rollback to previous image tag
kubectl set image deploy/runtime-canary runtime-container=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:3.0.8 --namespace=redwood-serving-canary
kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime-canary --namespace=redwood-serving-canary
```

jamie: can we get a light canary smoke before 22:00? 10min run at 21:50 to catch obvious issues.

keith: yep scheduling 21:50 quick smoke. I'll post results here.

alex: I'll watch dashboards and alerting. tagging @oncall-telemetry.

ops-bot: Deploy window reserved: 2026-03-17T22:00:00Z — reservation id rsv-7782.

keith: ACK. Will post "started" and "done" markers. If anything odd, will roll back immediately. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks all — please react with :thumbsup: if you can be online for the canary window or :warning: if you cannot.

alex: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

rhett: :thumbsup:

keith: started quick smoke at 21:50 — running now, will post metrics snapshot in ~6m.

keith: quick smoke results: 10m run, 500 requests, p95 gen latency +4% vs baseline, no 5xx, kv-cache hit rate steady. good to proceed to main window.

jamie: great — proceeding with 22:00 canary. I'll update if anything changes.

(End of thread)
